h1: Senior Backend Engineer at Northwind Data
label: Northwind Data
description: How I built and ran the event-ingestion team at Northwind Data, and what I would do differently.
intro: Northwind Data hired me in 2021 to make a fragile nightly batch job boring. That took three years and one rewrite.

faqs.a: Six engineers at the end, split across ingestion and platform.
The platform moved into maintenance mode and I wanted another hard migration.

blocks.text: I owned the event-ingestion path from the collector to the warehouse tables, and I led the team that kept it running.
What the pipeline looked like on day one

items: One nightly job that ran for six hours and failed about twice a week.
No replay path: a bad deploy meant re-sending events by hand.
Alerting that fired after the job had already missed its window.

items.title: Make failures visible
items.text: Added per-stage metrics and a replay endpoint before touching throughput.

items.title: Move to streaming
items.text: Migrated the collector to an at-least-once stream with idempotent writes.

items.title: Delete the old job
items.text: Ran both paths in parallel for two weeks, then removed the nightly batch.

blocks.title: The number that mattered
blocks.text: Missed delivery windows fell from roughly two per week to none in the last year.

blocks.title: What I would repeat
items: Ship a replay path before a faster path.
Run the old and new systems side by side until the numbers agree.
